   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">In <em style="font: inherit;">2020,</em> the increase in the allowance is a result of stress on our loan portfolio from the increase in unemployment and other negative effects of the coronavirus pandemic. Based on current economic indicators, the Company increased the economic qualitative factors within the allowance for loan losses evaluation. Relative to the number of requests for modifications and deferrals from commercial borrowers, additional COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> factors were applied to these loans after segmenting into industry classifications.&#xa0;&#xa0;Such requests from consumers were insignificant. The amount of net charge-offs also impacts the provision charged to operations for any category of loans. Charge-offs affect the historical rate applied to each category, and the amount needed to replenish the amount charged-off, which primarily&#xa0;impacted consumer loans. The total allowance reflects management&#x2019;s estimate of loan losses inherent in the loan portfolio at the Consolidated Balance Sheet date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">In <em style="font: inherit;">2019,</em> the allowance for commercial loans includes an amount for a single loan impairment, otherwise the provision decreased modestly from the prior year. The decrease in the provision for commercial real estate loans is due mainly to a decrease in the concentration of credit factor. The&#xa0;segmentation of the commercial real estate loan portfolio into its <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> largest concentrations&#xa0;resulted in lower allocations to those segments. The residential real estate, consumer-home equity and other household provisions remained fairly constant.&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">In <em style="font: inherit;">2018,</em> the commercial charge-off is&#xa0;related to loans that were restructured with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> principal forgiveness with a new borrowing relationship, but with a substantial concession in interest rate.&#xa0;&#xa0;The below market rate triggered recognition of a charge-off equivalent to the difference in present value of loan payments discounted at the market rate of interest.&#xa0;&#xa0;The charged off amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70924919" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="cldb:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossesWriteOffsRecordedAsLoanDiscount" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction> million is recorded as a loan discount.&#xa0;&#xa0;As loan payments are made, interest will be recognized at the market rate versus the negotiated rate via the amortization of the discount over the various lives of the loans. There was $<ix:nonFraction id="c70924920" contextRef="i_2018-12-31_AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis-RestructuredLoansWithNoPrincipalForgivenessMember_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableAllowance" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">625,000</ix:nonFraction> in specific reserve previously allocated to these loans at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2018</em>.&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The following tables represent credit exposures by internally assigned grades for years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>, respectively. The grading analysis estimates the capability of the borrower to repay the contractual obligations of the loan agreements as scheduled or at all. The Company&#x2019;s internal credit risk grading system is based on experiences with similarly graded loans.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Company&#x2019;s internally assigned grades are as follows:</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;text-indent:0;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:5.7%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:3.3%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#x2022;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:91%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i>Pass</i>&#xa0;&#x2013; loans which are protected by the current net worth and paying capacity of the obligor or by the value of the underlying collateral. Within this category, there are grades of exceptional, quality, acceptable and pass monitor.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;text-indent:0;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:5.7%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:3.3%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#x2022;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:91%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i>Special Mention </i>&#x2013; loans where a potential weakness or risk exists, which could cause a more serious problem if <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> corrected.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;text-indent:0;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:5.7%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:3.3%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#x2022;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:91%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i>Substandard</i>&#xa0;&#x2013; loans that have a well-defined weakness based on objective evidence and are characterized by the distinct possibility that the Bank will sustain some loss if the deficiencies are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> corrected.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;text-indent:0;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:5.7%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:3.3%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#x2022;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:91%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i>Doubtful </i>&#x2013; loans classified as doubtful have all the weaknesses inherent in a substandard asset but with the severity which makes collection in full highly questionable and improbable, based on existing circumstances.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;text-indent:0;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:5.7%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:3.3%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#x2022;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:91%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i>Loss</i>&#xa0;&#x2013; loans classified as a loss are considered uncollectible, or of such value that continuance as an asset is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> warranted. This rating does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> mean that the assets have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> recovery or salvage value but rather that the assets should be charged off now, even though partial or full recovery <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be possible in the future.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Company evaluates the classification of consumer, home equity and residential loans primarily on a pooled basis. If the Company becomes aware that adverse or distressed conditions exist that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>affect a particular loan, the loan is downgraded following the above definitions of special mention and substandard.&#xa0;&#xa0;Nonaccrual loans in these categories are evaluated for charge off or charge down, and the remaining balance has the same allowance factor as pooled loans.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Loans are considered to be nonperforming when they become <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="cldb:NumberOfDaysLoansArePastDueToBeOnNonaccrualStatus" id="c70924933" format="ixt-sec:durday">90</ix:nonNumeric> days past due or on nonaccrual status, though the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be receiving partial payments of interest and partial repayments of principal on such loans. When a loan is placed in non-accrual status, previously accrued but unpaid interest is recorded against interest income. Loans in foreclosure are considered nonperforming. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em>, there were $<ix:nonFraction id="c70924934" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:MortgageLoansInProcessOfForeclosureAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">604,000</ix:nonFraction> of loans in the process of foreclosure.</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Troubled Debt Restructuring </span></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Nonperforming loans also include certain loans that have been modified in troubled debt restructurings (TDRs) where economic concessions have been granted to borrowers who have experienced or are expected to experience financial difficulties. These concessions typically result from the Company&#x2019;s loss mitigation activities and could include reductions in the interest rate, payment extensions, forgiveness of principal, forbearance or other actions. Certain TDRs are classified as nonperforming at the time of restructure and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>only be returned to performing status after considering the borrower&#x2019;s sustained repayment performance for a reasonable period, generally <em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The <ix:nonFraction id="c70924950" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableModificationsNumberOfContracts2" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">seven</ix:nonFraction> commercial loans were all to <ix:nonFraction id="c70924951" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cldb:FinancingReceivableNumberOfNewBorrowingRelationships" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">one</ix:nonFraction> new borrowing relationship.&#xa0;&#xa0;The loans were restructured with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> principal forgiveness, but with a substantial concession in interest rate.&#xa0;&#xa0;The below market rate triggered recognition of a charge-off equivalent to the difference in present value of loan payments discounted at the market rate of interest.&#xa0;&#xa0;The charged off amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70924954" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="cldb:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossesWriteOffsRecordedAsLoanDiscount" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction> million is recorded as loan discount.&#xa0;&#xa0;As loan payments are made, interest will be recognized at the market rate versus the negotiated rate via the amortization of the discount over the various lives of the loans.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 22, 2020, </em>federal banking regulators issued an interagency statement that included guidance on their approach for the accounting of loan modifications in light of the economic impact of the Coronavirus Disease <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> (COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em>) pandemic. The guidance interprets current accounting standards and indicates that a lender can conclude that a borrower is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> experiencing financial difficulty if short-term modifications are made in response to COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19,</em> such as payment deferrals, fee waivers, extensions of repayment terms, or other delays in payment that are insignificant related to the loans in which the borrower is less than <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="cldb:MaximumNumberOfDaysPastDueOnContractualPaymentsForBorrowerNotExperiencingFinancialDifficulty" id="c70924960" format="ixt-sec:duryear">30</ix:nonNumeric> days past due on its contractual payments as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2019. </em>The agencies confirmed in working with the staff of the FASB that short-term modifications made on a good faith basis in response to COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> to borrowers who were current prior to any relief are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> TDRs.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December&#xa0;</em><em style="font: inherit;">31,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2020,</em> we had <ix:nonFraction id="c70924967" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cldb:FinancingReceivableNumberOfPaymentDeferrals" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">9</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;commercial loans aggregating $<ix:nonFraction id="c70924969" contextRef="i_2020-01-01_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="cldb:FinancingReceivableDeferredPayments" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6">18</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million, deferring principal and/or interest for periods ranging from <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="cldb:FinancingReceivableDeferredPaymentsPeriod" id="c70924970" format="ixt-sec:durday">90</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="cldb:FinancingReceivableDeferredPaymentsPeriod" id="c70924972" format="ixt-sec:durday">180</ix:nonNumeric> days.&#xa0;&#xa0;All of these loans were performing in accordance with their terms prior to modification, are currently performing, and are in conformance with the guidelines of the CARES Act. Since <em style="font: inherit;"> April&#xa0;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2020,</em> <ix:nonFraction id="c70924975" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="cldb:FinancingReceivablePriorModificationsNumberOfContractsReturnedToFullPayments" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">118</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;prior modifications aggregating $<ix:nonFraction id="c70924976" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="cldb:FinancingReceivablePriorModificationsAggregatingAmountReturnedToFullPaymentStatus" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6">105</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million have returned to full payment status. For further discussion, see Significant Developments Impact of COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> section of Item <em style="font: inherit;">7.</em> Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operation.&#xa0;</p>

text-align: right; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; border-bottom: 3px double rgb(0, 0, 0);"><ix:nonFraction id="c70925439" contextRef="i_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestment90DaysPastDueAndStillAccruing" scale="3" format="ixt:zerodash" decimals="-3">&#x2014;</ix:nonFraction></td><td style="width: 1%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; padding-bottom: 3px; margin-left: 0pt;">&#xa0;</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   </ix:continuation>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">An impaired loan is a loan on which, based on current information and events, it is probable that the Company will be unable to collect all amounts due (including both interest and principal) according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement. However, an insignificant delay or insignificant shortfall in amount of payments on a loan does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> indicate that the loan is impaired.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">When a loan is determined to be impaired, impairment should be measured based on the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#x2019;s effective interest rate. However, as a practical expedient, the Company will measure impairment based on a loan&#x2019;s observable market price, or the fair value of the collateral if the loan is collateral dependent.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Commercial loans and commercial real estate loans evaluated for impairment are excluded from the general pool of loans in the ALLL calculation regardless if a specific reserve was determined. If management determines that the value of the impaired loan is less than the recorded investment in the loan (net of previous charge-offs, deferred loan fees or costs and unamortized premium or discount), impairment is recognized through an allowance estimate or a charge-off to the allowance.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTE&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">7</em> - SUBORDINATED DEBT </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2007, </em>a trust formed by the Company issued $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926068" contextRef="d_2007-07-01_2007-07-31_LegalEntityAxis-TrustFormedByCompanyMember" unitRef="USD" name="cldb:FloatingRateTrustPreferredSecuritiesIssuedDuringPeriod" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6">5.0</ix:nonFraction> million of floating rate trust preferred securities as part of a pooled offering of such securities due <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2037. </em>The Company owns all $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926069" contextRef="i_2007-07-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-TrustCommonSecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="cldb:InvestmentInSecurities" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">155,000</ix:nonFraction> of the common securities issued by the trust. The securities bear interest at the <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>-month LIBOR rate plus <ix:nonFraction id="c70926071" contextRef="d_2007-07-01_2007-07-31_LegalEntityAxis-TrustFormedByCompanyMember_VariableRateAxis-LondonInterbankOfferedRateLIBORMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cldb:SecuritiesBasisSpreadOnVariableRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="4">1.45</ix:nonFraction>%. The rates at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> were <ix:nonFraction id="c70926073" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_LegalEntityAxis-TrustFormedByCompanyMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cldb:SecuritiesInterestRateEffectivePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="4">1.67</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction id="c70926074" contextRef="i_2019-12-31_LegalEntityAxis-TrustFormedByCompanyMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cldb:SecuritiesInterestRateEffectivePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="4">3.34</ix:nonFraction>%, respectively. The Company issued subordinated debentures to the trust in exchange for the proceeds of the trust preferred offering. The debentures represent the sole assets of this trust. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>redeem the subordinated debentures, in whole or in part, at par.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The trust is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> consolidated with the Company&#x2019;s financial statements. Accordingly, the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> report the securities issued by the trust as liabilities, but instead reports as liabilities the subordinated debentures issued by the Company and held by the trust. The subordinated debentures qualify as Tier&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital for regulatory purposes in determining and evaluating the Company&#x2019;s capital adequacy.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c1786659" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTE&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">8</em> &#x2013; COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Historically, the Bank has been&#xa0;required to maintain a certain level of aggregate cash reserves in order to satisfy federal regulatory requirements. These reserves could be&#xa0;held in useable vault cash and interest-earning balances at the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2019, </em>the Bank was required to maintain $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926079" contextRef="i_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashReserveDepositRequiredAndMade" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6">6.0</ix:nonFraction> million in cash reserves. However, in <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2020 </em>in response to the Covid-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> pandemic, the Federal Reserve eliminated the reserve requirement.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Bank grants commercial and industrial loans, commercial and residential mortgage loans, and consumer loans to customers in Northeastern Ohio and Western Pennsylvania. Although the Bank has a diversified portfolio, exposure to credit loss can be adversely impacted by downturns in local economic and employment conditions. Approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c70926081" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="cldb:PercentageOfUnsecuredLoans" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="3">8.4</ix:nonFraction>% of total loans are unsecured at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em> and approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c70926082" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="cldb:PercentageOfUnsecuredLoans" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="4">0.23</ix:nonFraction>% at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2019</em>. The increase from the prior year is due to loans granted under the PPP that are fully guaranteed by the SBA, as previously disclosed.&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Bank is a party to financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers. These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit, standby letters of credit and financial guarantees. Such instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit risk in excess of the amount recognized on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. The contract or notional amounts on those instruments reflect the extent of involvement the Company has in particular classes of financial instruments.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">In the event of nonperformance by the other party, the Company&#x2019;s exposure to credit loss on these financial instruments is represented by the contract or notional amount of the instrument. The Company uses the same credit policies in making commitments and conditional obligations as it does for instruments recorded on the balance sheet. The amount and nature of collateral obtained, if any, is based on management&#x2019;s credit evaluation.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> violation of any condition established in the contract. Generally, these financial arrangements have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>require payment of a fee. Standby letters of credit are conditional commitments issued by the Company to guarantee the performance of a customer to a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party. Since many of the commitments are expected to expire without being drawn upon, the total commitment amounts do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily represent future cash requirements. The Company evaluates each customer&#x2019;s creditworthiness on a case-by-case basis. The amount of collateral obtained, if deemed necessary by the Company upon extension of credit, is based on management&#x2019;s credit evaluation of the counterparty. Collateral held varies but <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include accounts receivable, inventory, property, plant and equipment and income-producing commercial properties. The increase in commitments is in line with the Company&#x2019;s increased focus on commercial and industrial lending, and specifically lines of credit.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Company also offers limited overdraft protection as a non-contractual courtesy which is available to businesses as well as individually/jointly owned accounts in good standing for personal or household use. The Company reserves the right to discontinue this service without prior notice.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Customer Derivatives - Interest Rate Swaps/Floors &#x2013; The Company enters into interest rate swaps that allow our commercial loan customers to effectively convert a variable-rate commercial loan agreement to a fixed-rate commercial loan agreement. Under these agreements, the Company enters into a variable-rate loan agreement with a customer in addition to an interest rate swap agreement, which serves to effectively swap the customer&#x2019;s variable-rate into a fixed-rate. The Company then enters into a corresponding swap agreement with a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party in order to economically hedge its exposure through the customer agreement. The interest rate swaps with both the customers and <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedges under FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815</em> and are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> marked to market through earnings. As the interest rate swaps are structured to offset each other, changes to the underlying benchmark interest rates considered in the valuation of these instruments do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> result in an impact to earnings; however, there <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be fair value adjustments related to credit quality variations between counterparties, which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>impact earnings as required by FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820.</em> There was <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> effect on earnings in any periods presented. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em>, based upon the swap contract values, the company had <ix:nonFraction id="c70926095" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="cldb:NumberOfSecuritiesOwnedAndPledgedAsCollateral" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">four</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;U.S. Government-sponsored mortgage-backed securities pledged for collateral on its interest rate swaps with a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party financial institution with a fair value $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926097" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SecurityOwnedAndPledgedAsCollateralFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">4.7</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million. At&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2019</em>, based upon the swap contract values, the company had <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70926098">two</span>&#xa0;U.S. Government-sponsored mortgage-backed securities pledged for collateral on its interest rate swaps with a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party financial institution with a fair value $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926100" contextRef="i_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SecurityOwnedAndPledgedAsCollateralFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">2.8</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTE&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">9</em> &#x2013; BENEFIT PLANS </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Bank has a contributory defined contribution retirement plan (<em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) plan) which covers substantially all employees. Total expense under the plan was $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926285" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">396,000</ix:nonFraction> for <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926287" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">367,000</ix:nonFraction> for <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926289" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">337,000</ix:nonFraction> for <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>. The Bank matches participants&#x2019; voluntary contributions up to <ix:nonFraction id="c70926291" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">5</ix:nonFraction>% of gross pay. Participants were able to make voluntary contributions to the plan up to a maximum of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926292" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanMaximumAnnualContributionsPerEmployeeAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">19,000</ix:nonFraction> with an additional $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926293" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="cldb:AdditionalCatchUpDeferralForPlanParticipantsOverAge50" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">6,000</ix:nonFraction> catch-up deferral for plan participants over the age of <em style="font: inherit;">50.</em> The Bank makes bi-weekly contributions to this plan equal to amounts accrued for plan expense.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Company provides supplemental retirement benefit plans for the benefit of certain officers and non-officer directors. The plan for officers is designed to provide post-retirement benefits to supplement other sources of retirement income such as social security and <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) benefits. The benefits will be paid for a period of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" name="cldb:DefinedBenefitPlanPaymentDurationAfterRetirement" id="c70926296" format="ixt-sec:duryear">15</ix:nonNumeric> years after retirement. Director Retirement Agreements provide for a benefit of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926297" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RetirementPlanNameAxis-DirectorsPlanMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="cldb:DefinedBenefitPlanAnnualPaymentAfterRetirement" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">10,000</ix:nonFraction> annually on or after the director reaches normal retirement age, which is based on a combination of age and years of service. Director retirement benefits are paid over a period of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_RetirementPlanNameAxis-DirectorsPlanMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" name="cldb:DefinedBenefitPlanPaymentDurationAfterRetirement" id="c70926298" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric>&#xa0;years following retirement. The Company accrues the cost of these post-retirement benefits during the working careers of the officers and directors. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em>, the accumulated liability for these benefits totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926299" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanBenefitObligation" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">4.1</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million, with $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926300" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RetirementPlanNameAxis-OfficersPlanMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanBenefitObligation" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">3.6</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million accrued for the officers&#x2019; plan and $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926301" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RetirementPlanNameAxis-DirectorsPlanMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanBenefitObligation" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">521,000</ix:nonFraction> for the directors&#x2019; plan.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Supplemental executive retirement agreements are unfunded plans and have <ix:nonFraction id="c70926303" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-ExecutiveOfficerMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanFairValueOfPlanAssets" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> plan assets. The benefit obligation represents the vested net present value of future payments to individuals under the agreements. The benefit expense, as specified in the agreements for the entire year <em style="font: inherit;">2021,</em> is expected to be approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926305" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-ExecutiveOfficerMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanExpectedFutureEmployerContributionsCurrentFiscalYear" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">555,000</ix:nonFraction>. The benefits expected to be paid in the next year are approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926306" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-ExecutiveOfficerMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanExpectedFutureBenefitPaymentsNextTwelveMonths" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">107,000</ix:nonFraction>.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Bank has purchased insurance contracts on the lives of the participants in the supplemental retirement benefit plan and has named the Bank as the beneficiary. Similarly, the Company has purchased insurance contracts on the lives of the directors with the Bancorp as beneficiary. While <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> direct linkage exists between the supplemental retirement benefit plan and the life insurance contracts, it is management&#x2019;s current intent that the revenue from the insurance contracts be used as a funding source for the plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Company accrues for the monthly benefit expense of postretirement cost of insurance for split-dollar life insurance coverage. A valuation allowance of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70926345" contextRef="i_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">28,000</ix:nonFraction> was established in <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>&#xa0;to offset in its entirety capital losses.&#xa0;&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Company prescribes a recognition threshold and a measurement attribute for the financial statement recognition and measurement of a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax return. Benefits from tax positions should be recognized in the financial statements only when it is more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the tax position will be sustained upon examination by the appropriate taxing authority that would have full knowledge of all relevant information. A tax position that meets the more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognition threshold is measured at the largest amount of benefit that is greater than <em style="font: inherit;">fifty</em> percent likely of being realized upon ultimate settlement. Tax positions that previously failed to meet the more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognition threshold should be recognized in the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> subsequent financial reporting period in which that threshold is met. Previously recognized tax positions that <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer meet the more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognition threshold should be derecognized in the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> subsequent financial reporting period in which that threshold is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer met. The provision also provides guidance on the accounting for and disclosure of unrecognized tax benefits, interest and penalties. There were <ix:nonFraction id="c70926374" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SignificantChangeInUnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIsReasonablyPossibleAmountOfUnrecordedBenefit" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> significant unrecognized tax benefits at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em> and the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect any significant increase in unrecognized tax benefits in the next <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months. <ix:nonFraction id="c70926377" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationPenaltiesAndInterestAccrued" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">No</ix:nonFraction> interest or penalties were incurred for income taxes which would have been recorded as a component of income tax expense.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">There is currently <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> liability for uncertain tax positions and <ix:nonFraction id="c70926379" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> known unrecognized tax benefits. The Company&#x2019;s federal and state income tax returns for taxable years through <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70926380"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70926381">2016</span></span>&#xa0;have been closed for purposes of examination by the Internal Revenue Service and the Ohio Department of Revenue.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c1786672" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">11</em> &#x2013; FAIR VALUE </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Measurements </span></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Company groups assets and liabilities recorded at fair value into <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels based on the markets in which the assets and liabilities are traded and the reliability of the assumptions used to determine fair value. A financial instrument&#x2019;s level within the fair value hierarchy is based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement (with level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> considered highest and level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> considered lowest). A brief description of each level follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:92%;text-indent:0;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:7.7%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Level&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">1:</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:1%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:91.3%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Quoted prices are available in active markets for identical assets or liabilities as of the reported date.</p> </td></tr>
<tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:7.7%;">&#xa0;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:1%;">&#xa0;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:91.3%;">&#xa0;</td></tr>
<tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:7.7%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:1%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:91.3%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Pricing inputs are other than quoted prices in active markets, which are either directly or indirectly observable as of the reported date. The nature of these assets and liabilities include items for which quoted prices are available but which trade less frequently, and items that are fair valued using other financial instruments, the parameters of which can be directly observed.</p> </td></tr>
<tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:7.7%;">&#xa0;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:1%;">&#xa0;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:91.3%;">&#xa0;</td></tr>
<tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:7.7%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:1%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:91.3%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Assets and liabilities that have little to <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> pricing observability as of the reported date. These items do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-way markets and are measured using management&#x2019;s best estimate of fair value, where inputs into the determination of fair value require significant management judgment or estimation.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The following table presents the assets reported on the consolidated balance sheets at their fair value as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2019</em> by level within the fair value hierarchy. Financial assets and liabilities are classified in their entirety based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The following tables present the changes in the Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> fair value category for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>. The Company classifies financial instruments in Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> of the fair-value hierarchy when there is reliance on at least <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> significant unobservable input to the valuation model. In addition to these unobservable inputs, the valuation models for Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> financial instruments typically also rely on a number of inputs that are readily observable either directly or indirectly.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Company conducts OTTI analyses on a quarterly basis. The initial indication of other-than-temporary impairment for both debt and equity securities is a decline in the fair value below the amount recorded for an investment. A decline in value that is considered to be other-than-temporary is recorded as a loss within non-interest income in the Consolidated Statements of Income. In determining whether an impairment is other than temporary, the Company considers a number of factors, including, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, the length of time and extent to which the market value has been less than cost, recent events specific to the issuer, including investment downgrades by rating agencies and economic conditions of its industry, and a determination that the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> intend to sell those investments and it is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the Company will be required to sell the investments before recovery of its amortized cost basis less any current period credit loss. Among the factors that are considered in determining the Company&#x2019;s intent and ability is a review of its capital adequacy, interest rate risk position and liquidity.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Company also considers the issuer&#x2019;s financial condition, capital strength and near-term prospects. In addition, for debt securities the Company considers the cause of the price decline (general level of interest rates and industry- and issuer-specific factors), current ability to make future payments in a timely manner and the issuer&#x2019;s ability to service debt, the assessment of a security&#x2019;s ability to recover any decline in market value, the ability of the issuer to meet contractual obligations and the Company&#x2019;s intent and ability to retain the security. All of the foregoing require considerable judgment.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Financial Instruments </span></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Company discloses fair value information about financial instruments, whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognized in the Consolidated Balance Sheets, for which it is practicable to estimate the value. In cases where quoted market prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are based on estimates using present value or other estimation techniques. Those techniques are significantly affected by the assumptions used, including the discount rate and estimates of future cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Such techniques and assumptions, as they apply to individual categories of the financial instruments, are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Investment securities available for sale &#x2013; Fair values of securities are based on quoted market prices, where available.&#xa0;If quoted market prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are based on quoted market prices of comparable securities. Prices on trust preferred securities were calculated using a discounted cash-flow technique. Cash flows were estimated based on credit and prepayment assumptions. The present value of the projected cash flows was calculated using a discount rate equal to the current yield used to accrete the beneficial interest.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Loans held for sale &#x2013; Loans held for sale consist of residential mortgage loans originated for sale. Loans held for sale are recorded at fair value based on what the secondary markets have offered on best efforts commitments.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Interest rate derivatives &#x2013; The fair value is based on settlement values adjusted for credit risks associated with the counter parties and the Company and observable market interest rate curves.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">In addition, other assets and liabilities of the Company that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> defined as financial instruments are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> included in the disclosures, such as property and equipment. Also, non-financial instruments typically <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognized in financial statements nevertheless <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have value but are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> included in the above disclosures. These include, among other items, the estimated earning power of core deposit accounts, the trained work force, customer goodwill and similar items. Accordingly, the aggregate fair value amounts presented do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> represent the underlying value of the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTE&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">12</em> - ACCUMULATED OTHER COMPREHENSIVE INCOME (LOSS)</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:RegulatoryCapitalRequirementsUnderBankingRegulationsTextBlock" id="c1786683" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTE&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">13</em> - REGULATORY MATTERS </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Company and the Bank are subject to regulatory capital requirements administered by federal banking agencies. Capital adequacy guidelines and prompt corrective action regulations involve quantitative measures of assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance-sheet items calculated under regulatory accounting practices. Capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgments by regulators about components, risk weightings, and other factors, and the regulators can lower classifications in certain cases. Failure to meet various capital requirements can initiate regulatory action that could have a direct material effect on the financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The prompt corrective action regulations provide <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> categories, including well capitalized, adequately capitalized, undercapitalized, significantly undercapitalized, and critically undercapitalized, although these terms are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> used to represent overall financial condition. If a bank is only adequately capitalized, regulatory approval is required to, among other things, accept, renew or roll-over brokered deposits. If a bank is undercapitalized, capital distributions and growth and expansion are limited, and plans for capital restoration are required.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2013, </em>the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve Board and the FDIC approved the final rules implementing the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's capital guidelines for U.S. banks and their holding companies (commonly known as Basel III). Under the final rules, which began for the Company and the Bank on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2015 </em>and are subject to a phase-in period through <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2019, </em>minimum requirements increased for both the quantity and quality of capital held by the Company and the Bank. The rules included a new common equity Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital to risk-weighted assets ratio (<em style="font: inherit;">CET1</em> ratio) of <em style="font: inherit;">4.5%</em> and a capital conservation buffer of <em style="font: inherit;">2.5%</em> of risk-weighted assets, which when fully phased-in, effectively resulted&#xa0;in a minimum <em style="font: inherit;">CET1</em> ratio of <em style="font: inherit;">7.0%.</em> Basel III raises the minimum ratio of Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital to risk-weighted assets from <em style="font: inherit;">4.0%</em> to <em style="font: inherit;">6.0%</em> (which, with the capital conservation buffer, effectively resulted&#xa0;in a minimum Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital ratio of <em style="font: inherit;">8.5%</em> when fully phased-in), effectively resulted&#xa0;in a minimum total capital to risk-weighted assets ratio of <em style="font: inherit;">10.5%</em> (with the capital conservation buffer fully phased-in), and required&#xa0;a minimum leverage ratio of <em style="font: inherit;">4.0%.</em> Basel III also made&#xa0;changes to risk weights for certain assets and off-balance-sheet exposures. Management expects that the capital ratios for the Company and the Bank under Basel III will continue to exceed the well capitalized minimum capital requirements, as they currently exceed the fully phased in <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> requirements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>

   </ix:exclude>
   <ix:exclude>&#xa0;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The capital conservation buffers of <em style="font: inherit;">2.5%</em> above the minimum common equity Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital, Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital and total risk-based capital ratios are required in order to avoid limitations on capital distributions, including dividend payments, and certain discretionary bonus payments. A banking organization with a buffer of less than the required amount would be subject to increasingly stringent limitations on such distributions and payments as the buffer approaches zero.&#xa0; The new rule also generally prohibits a banking organization from making such distributions or payments during any quarter if its eligible retained income is negative and its capital conservation buffer ratio was <em style="font: inherit;">2.5%</em> or less at the end of the previous quarter.&#xa0; The eligible retained income of a banking organization is defined as its net income for the <em style="font: inherit;">four</em> calendar quarters preceding the current calendar quarter, based on the organization&#x2019;s quarterly regulatory reports, net of any distributions and associated tax effects <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> already reflected in net income.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">In addition to the capital requirements for bank holding companies generally, financial holding companies are also required to meet &#x201c;well-capitalized&#x201d; requirements of the Federal Reserve Board. A bank holding company or financial holding company that is covered by the Federal Reserve&#x2019;s Small Bank Holding Company Policy is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> required to comply with the consolidated capital requirements, although its bank subsidiaries still must comply with the applicable capital requirements. As a bank holding company with assets of less than <em style="font: inherit;">$1</em> billion and meeting certain other requirements, the Company is covered by the Small Bank Holding Company Policy.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2019</em>, actual capital levels and minimum required levels for the Company, if it were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> covered by the Small Bank Holding Company Policy, were:</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">16</em> - DIVIDEND RESTRICTIONS </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Bank is subject to a dividend restriction that generally limits the amount of dividends that can be paid by an Ohio state-chartered bank. Under the Ohio Banking Code, cash dividends <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exceed net profits as defined for that year combined with retained net profits for the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> preceding years less any required transfers to surplus. Under this formula, the amount available for payment of dividends in <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> is $<ix:nonFraction id="c70927058" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StatutoryAccountingPracticesStatutoryAmountAvailableForDividendPaymentsWithRegulatoryApproval" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">7.7</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million plus <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> profits retained up to the date of the dividend declaration.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTE&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> &#x2013; EQUITY COMPENSATION</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">During <em style="font: inherit;">2015,</em> the Company, created the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> Omnibus Equity Plan and The Director Equity Plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The Omnibus Equity Plan permits the award of up to <ix:nonFraction id="c70927083" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember_PlanNameAxis-OmnibusEquityPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">340,000</ix:nonFraction> shares to the Company&#x2019;s employees to promote the long-term financial success of the Company, increasing shareholder value by providing employees the opportunity to acquire an ownership interest in the Company and enabling the Company and its related entities to attract and retain the services of those upon whom the successful conduct of business depends. There were <ix:nonFraction id="c70927084" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember_PlanNameAxis-OmnibusEquityPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">47,567</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;restricted Board approved shares granted under the plan in calendar <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> and <ix:nonFraction id="c70927086" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember_PlanNameAxis-OmnibusEquityPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">30,156</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;restricted Board approved shares granted under the plan in calendar <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>. The Company is expensing the grant date fair value of all share-based compensation over the requisite vesting periods on a prorated straight-line basis.&#xa0;&#xa0;In <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>, compensation expense of $<ix:nonFraction id="c70927090" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember_PlanNameAxis-OmnibusEquityPlanMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">403,000</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c70927091" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember_PlanNameAxis-OmnibusEquityPlanMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">740,000</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, was recorded in the Consolidated Statements of Income. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em>, there was $<ix:nonFraction id="c70927092" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember_PlanNameAxis-OmnibusEquityPlanMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognized" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">581,000</ix:nonFraction> of total unrecognized compensation expense related to the non-vested shares granted under the Plan.&#xa0;Shares awarded under this plan can vest immediately and/or on the anniversary of the award date from <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70927093">one</span> to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c70927094">three</span> years out if the employee remains employed with Cortland Bancorp. The remaining cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember_PlanNameAxis-OmnibusEquityPlanMember" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedPeriodForRecognition1" id="c70927095" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">20.6</ix:nonNumeric>&#xa0;months. &#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Granted shares are awarded upon meeting achievement of performance objectives derived from <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more of the performance criteria.&#xa0;The main metrics used for the periods presented were <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year earnings per share growth, <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year return on equity,&#xa0;and <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year total shareholder return each ranked versus a peer group.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTE&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">20</em> &#x2013; LEASES</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Operating leases in which the Company is the lessee are recorded as operating lease Right of Use (&#x201c;ROU&#x201d;) assets and operating lease liabilities, included in other assets and other liabilities, respectively, on the consolidated balance sheets. The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently have any significant finance leases in which it is the lessee. Operating lease ROU assets represent the Company&#x2019;s right to use an underlying asset during the lease term and operating lease liabilities represent the obligation to make lease payments arising from the lease. The Company elected to adopt the transition method, which uses a modified retrospective transition approach. ROU assets and operating lease liabilities are recognized as of the date of adoption based on the present value of the remaining lease payments using a discount rate that represents the incremental borrowing rate at the date of initial application. Operating lease expense, which is comprised of amortization of the ROU asset and the implicit interest accreted on the operating lease liability, is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term, and is recorded in occupancy and equipment expense in the consolidated statements of income and other comprehensive income. The Company leases relate primarily to office space and bank branches with remaining lease terms of generally <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRemainingLeaseTerm" id="c70927126" format="ixt-sec:duryear">5</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRemainingLeaseTerm" id="c70927127" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years. Certain lease arrangements contain extension options which typically range from <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" id="c70927128" format="ixt-sec:duryear">5</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" id="c70927129" format="ixt-sec:duryear">15</ix:nonNumeric> years at the then fair market rental rates. As these extension options are generally considered reasonably certain of exercise, they are included in the lease term. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019,</em>&#xa0;operating lease ROU assets and liabilities were $<ix:nonFraction id="c70927131" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherAssetsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">1.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c70927132" contextRef="i_2019-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherAssetsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">1.8</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. For the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em>, the Company recognized $<ix:nonFraction id="c70927133" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseCost" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">229,000</ix:nonFraction> in operating lease cost, where in $<ix:nonFraction id="c70927134" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeasePayments" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">209,000</ix:nonFraction> is operating cash flows from operating leases and $<ix:nonFraction id="c70927135" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAssetAmortizationExpense" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">20,000</ix:nonFraction> is noncash expense amortization of the ROU asset and the implicit interest, respectively.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTE&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">21</em>&#xa0;&#x2013; RISKS AND UNCERTAINTIES</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The impact of the COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> pandemic is fluid and continues to evolve, adversely affecting many of the Company&#x2019;s customers. The pandemic and its associated impacts on trade, travel, employee productivity, unemployment, and consumer spending has resulted in less economic activity and volatility and disruption in the financial markets. The ultimate extent of the impact of the COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> pandemic on the Company&#x2019;s business, financial condition, and results of operations is currently uncertain and will depend on various developments and other factors, including, among others, the duration and scope of the pandemic, as well as governmental, regulatory, and private sector responses to the pandemic, and the associated impacts on the economy, financial markets and our customers, employees, and vendors. While the full effects of the pandemic remain unknown, the Company is committed to supporting its customers, employees, and communities during this difficult time.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</span>. With the supervision and participation by management, including the Company&#x2019;s principal executive officer and principal financial officer, the effectiveness of disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#x201c;Exchange Act&#x201d;)) has been evaluated as of the end of the period covered by this report. Based upon that evaluation, the Company&#x2019;s principal executive officer and principal financial officer have concluded that these controls and procedures were effective.</p>

Our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that there have been no changes during the fourth quarter of 2020 in the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules 13a-13 and 15d-15 of the Exchange Act) that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, internal control over financial reporting.</p>
